summary: This step is a package registry for prediction models: for each of 19 candidate models it recorded whether it is credible, whether it can legally be used for this case (licence check), and how much of the 39,286-record set it can actually score, then enabled the four that passed for the MVP (minimum viable product, the smallest end-to-end version) — AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, ESM1b (a protein language model) and REVEL (a live, per-request scoring service). AlphaMissense covers 27.0% of all records (67.9% of missense alleles), SpliceAI 82.8% (84.3% of alleles it targets), ESM1b 11.6% (29.2% of missense), and REVEL was sampled live at 52 of 200 alleles. A join-integrity check confirmed AlphaMissense and SpliceAI hit their pre-registered exact row counts (10,601 and 32,534), so nothing downstream rests on a broken `allele_id` join. The step also found that only SpliceAI can see both alleles of the confirmed BUB1B pair, and it reports no splice effect on either (scores 0.00 and 0.03) — a result recorded before steps 4-6 ran, not after.
why: A model roster has to be filtered before it is run, the same way a software team vets a third-party library before adding it as a dependency: license terms, whether the artifact can be downloaded at all, and whether it actually has data for the records at hand. Without this gate, step 3's inference layer would spend GPU/API budget calling models with near-zero coverage, and step 4's ranking would silently treat 'not scored' the same as 'scored as harmless' — the exact confusion the step 2 finding about the BUB1B pair heads off downstream.
verdict: H059 (`P4-2a`) supported at confidence 0.80: all four enabled lanes ran end-to-end on the record set in one day, and the two correctness gates (AlphaMissense/SpliceAI exact row counts) held. H060 (`P4-3`) refuted: AlphaMissense (67.9%) and ESM1b (29.2%) both fall below the 90% coverage bar, and even below the 70% line that would count as a genuine refutation rather than a near-miss — attributed to using iteration 2's narrower VEP-REST plugin pass rather than the full published AlphaMissense table, and to ESM1b's protein-accession namespace not matching the record set.

inherits.what: The registry can only report a coverage percentage against step 1's fixed 39,286-record set; without a stable denominator, 'AlphaMissense scores 10,601 alleles' would not mean anything. It also inherits step 1's unresolved uniprot gap directly and has to solve it itself, by building a protein-accession adapter that reaches ESM1b's table through the gene name and protein change instead.

hands_to.what: Step 3's inference API only calls the four lanes this step enabled and licensed; it reads `models.toml` as its worklist. It also inherits the finding that only SpliceAI has any opinion on the confirmed pair's stop-gained half, which is why step 3's per-lane score table for that allele has three blanks and one near-zero number rather than four numbers.
